'''Alexander Grigoryevich Abramov''' ({{langx|ru|Александр Григорьевич Абрамов}}, born 20 February 1959) is a Russian businessperson, who until March 2022 was the chairman of the board of directors of [[Evraz]], one of Russia's largest steel producers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=CHANGES IN THE COMPOSITION OF THE BOARD|website=investegate.co.uk|date=|url=https://www.investegate.co.uk/evraz-plc--evr-/rns/changes-in-the-composition-of-the-board/202203110721094777E/|accessdate=|archive-date=9 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209111357/https://www.investegate.co.uk/evraz-plc--evr-/rns/changes-in-the-composition-of-the-board/202203110721094777E/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Since 1998, he has amassed one of the largest steel and iron empires in Russia, which employed 71,591 people around the world, with steel output of 13,57 million tones and turnover of $14,1 billion in 2021, leading to him be widely considered a [[Russian oligarch]]. A business partner and ally of [[Aleksandr Frolov (businessman)|Aleksandr Frolov]] and [[Roman Abramovich]], Abramov was in June 2021 listed by ''[[Forbes]]'' as having an estimated net worth of $8.0&nbsp;billion.<ref name=Forbes>{{Cite web|first= |last= |authorlink=   |title=Alexander Abramov   |website=[[Forbes - The World's Billionaires]]|date= |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/alexander-abramov/?sh=7b76074d7e72  |accessdate=June 13, 2021}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Abramov was born in 1959 in Moscow, Russia, USSR.<ref name=JPWorld>{{Cite news|first= |last= |authorlink=   |title= The world's 50 Richest Jews: 21–30  |newspaper=[[The Jerusalem Post]]|date=September 7, 2010 |url=https://www.jpost.com/jewish-world/jewish-features/the-worlds-50-richest-jews-21-30  |accessdate=}}</ref> He is of Jewish descent.<ref name=JPWorld/> He graduated from the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] with a degree in physics and mathematics.<ref name=JPWorld/><ref>[http://bio.fizteh.ru/graduate/years/1982.html DMCP graduates] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090126203911/http://bio.fizteh.ru/graduate/years/1982.html |date=26 January 2009 }}. [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] Class of 1982</ref> He first worked for Russia's space and defense program before becoming a metal trader after government funding declined.<ref name=JPWorld/>

==Career==
EVRAZ is a product of Russia's growth since the [[1998 Russian financial crisis|1998 financial crisis]] and Abramov is representative of the second wave of Russian magnates who went into business after the best assets had been taken. Unlike the first wave of politically connected oligarchs, such as [[Mikhail Khodorkovsky]] and [[Vladimir Potanin]], Abramov had neither political leverage nor financial resources to help him benefit from Russia's chaotic [[privatisation]] of the 1990s.

In the 2000s, Evraz-Holding has emerged as one of the most aggressive vertically integrated business groups in Russia and worldwide. Its assets now include ore mines and steel mills in Russia, steel mills in North America and Kazakhstan, as well as Russian coal company PJSC Raspadskaya.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Panibratov|first=Andrei|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=spYkjkCutyMC&q=Evraz-Holding+aggressive+vertically+integrated+business+groups+in+Russia&pg=PA108|title=Russian Multinationals: From Regional Supremacy to Global Lead|date=2012|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-0-415-61588-4|language=en}}</ref>

In June 2005, EvrazHolding was listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]]. Five months later, Abramov resigned as group president but remains a member of the board.<ref>{{cite web|title=Board of directors|url=https://www.evraz.com/governance/directors/|website=Evraz}}</ref> In 2019, Abramov alongside other directors, sold $160m worth of shares in the company.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Evraz shares lower after main owners sell another tranche for £158M|url=https://www.spglobal.com/marketintelligence/en/news-insights/trending/oGtx7HYWhdxxgIFI4m8zOA2|access-date=2021-01-08|website=www.spglobal.com|language=en-us}}</ref> He resigned from the board of EVRAZ plc in March 2022.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Evraz directors quit in wake of UK sanctions|url=https://www.ft.com/content/fcc0f2c7-e687-4d9d-986e-11a32bf481c1|access-date=|newspaper=Financial Times|date=11 March 2022 |language=}}</ref>

== Entrepreneurship==
===Trading===
He used his contacts with Russia's steel mills, which used high-temperature technologies, and offered his services not as a scientist but as a metal trader. Trading was a popular and quick way to make money in Russia in the early 1990s. The economy was shrinking, non-payment was a chronic problem and any offer of cash from a trader was welcomed by factories. By 1997, trading was less profitable and many trading companies, including Abramov's, were owed large sums by producers. Abramov began buying factories and [[debt restructuring|swapped debt for equity]] in the [[Nizhny Tagil]] steel mill, while also buying stakes in its rail-producing plant from other shareholders.{{citation needed|date=March 2025}}

===Acquisitions, monopolies and factories===
While the first wave of Russian oligarchs grabbed whatever assets they could, Mr Abramov acquired them in a much more focused way. He decided to build a monopoly for rail and steel construction products and looked for factories that would give him synergies. The only other big factories making these products were in the industrial region of [[Kemerovo]], also home to Russia's largest coalmines. Using his old trading contacts with coalmine bosses, Abramov was introduced to [[Aman Tuleev]], populist governor of the region.{{citation needed|date=March 2025}}

===Pitching job creation in the vacuum of bankrupt factories===
The two factories Abramov was interested in were in bankruptcy in 1998. Salaries had not been paid for up to eight months and strikes were breaking out.{{citation needed|date=March 2025}}

====The deal: managers for factories====
Tuleev needed good managers. Abramov needed the two factories and soon a deal was made.

As a state creditor, Tuleev would help appoint external managers loyal to EvrazHolding to run the steel mills. Abramov would pay salaries and taxes, guarantee jobs and support Tuleev's social projects.{{citation needed|date=March 2025}}

====Acquisitions====
In 2007, EVRAZ acquired [[Oregon Steel Mills]] and [[Claymont Steel]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rbc.ru/economics/10/12/2007/5703ca419a79470eaf7683a0
|title=Evraz Group приобретает Claymont Steel за $564 млн |author= |date= 2007-12-10|publisher= [[RBC Group]] |access-date=2023-05-26}}</ref>

==Sanctions==

Abramov is named in the [[Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act]] released by US Treasury in January 2018.<ref name="CAATSA">{{cite web |title=Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act |url=http://prod-upp-image-read.ft.com/40911a30-057c-11e8-9650-9c0ad2d7c5b5 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Treasury Releases CAATSA Reports, Including on Senior Foreign Political Figures and Oligarchs in the Russian Federation |date=16 January 2024 |url=https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sm0271 }}</ref>

He was sanctioned by the [[UK]] government in 2022 in relation to the [[Russo-Ukrainian War]].<ref>{{cite web |title=CONSOLIDATED LIST OF FINANCIAL SANCTIONS TARGETS IN THE UK |url=https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1150217/Russia.pdf |access-date=16 April 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is married with three children, and lives outside of Russia.<ref>{{Cite web|title= Russian billionaire launches legal action against Australia's foreign minister over sanctions|url= https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2022/jun/18/russian-billionaire-launches-legal-action-against-australias-foreign-minister-over-sanctions |website= theguardian.com |date= 17 June 2022 |language=en}}</ref> His hobbies include fishing, swimming, tennis.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Russian Olympians Foundation|url=http://www.olympians.ru/en/15/4837/5898|access-date=2021-04-22|website=www.olympians.ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tognini |first=Giacomo |title=Biden And Allies Are Coming For Russian Billionaires' Yachts: Forbes Tracked Down 32. Here's Where To Find Them |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/giacomotognini/2022/03/01/biden-and-allies-are-coming-for-russian-billionaires-yachts-forbes-tracked-down-32-heres-where-to-find-them/ |access-date=2022-03-03 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>
